correctness.rationale: At a 2+2-support line the four coefficients of the Fermat cubic on the Grassmann chart have linear parts 6A, 6E, 6B, 6F in the displayed order. For each branch's support constraints on C,D,G,H, the mixed cubic coefficients admit B=E=0 and the endpoint cubics solve separately; the implicit solution is unique. Thus these are exact branch ideals, not just tangent ideals. Intersecting (C,D), (G,H), (D,G), (C,H) gives (CG,DH). At any 2+3-support point let p and q lie in the pair and triple blocks and z be the unused coordinate. Linearized cubic constraints kill both variations in the pair-block complement, and constrain the two triple-block variations by the nonzero Fermat differential at q. The two surface tangent planes share precisely the elliptic tangent and have distinct free p-into-z and q-into-z directions. Their scheme intersection has dimension and embedding dimension one, hence is regular. The completed reduced union is the fiber product of the two smooth surface rings over the regular curve ring, giving C[[t,u,v]]/(uv). The completed Fitting ideals are the Jacobian minors computed using completed differentials: (u,v) at a double curve, and all six pairwise products in the regular ambient ring at a fourfold point. Both are radical, which descends by faithful flatness. The homogeneous local models have degrees 2 and 4, giving the asserted Hilbert–Samuel multiplicities. The four tangent planes are simultaneous coordinate planes: adjacent ones share an axis, not pairwise transverse in the fourfold ambient space. This is the geometry encoded by the stated ring. The frozen symbolic verifier and its recorded output were inspected, not executed.

The exact germs resolve the local intersection geometry on both singular strata and distinguish a reduced intrinsic singular scheme from a merely known reduced support.
